newsitem.title: JAPAN: US's Albright heads for China, last stop on trip.
newsitem.headline: US's Albright heads for China, last stop on trip.

text.p: Newly appointed U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright left Tokyo for China on Monday, the last stop of her whirlwind nine-nation tour, Japanese Foreign Ministry officials said.
Albright met Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto over breakfast on Monday morning before boarding her flight to Beijing.
In the Chinese capital, she will become one of the first foreign dignitaries to meet Chinese leaders since the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

But a senior U.S. State Department official travelling with her said Albright did not expect progress in major issues between the two countries -- human rights, trade, Taiwan, Hong Kong and nuclear non-proliferation.

"The emphasis in China over the coming weeks and months is likely to be on continuity, on stability within the leadership, on building consensus within the leadership, in other words nothing risky," said the senior U.S. State Department official, who briefed reporters on condition of anonymity.
"Our expectations should not be too high," he said.
